beats.narration: Hey Claude — If one endpoint absorbs tools, structured outputs, and server tools, where is the real seam — the line past which you stop controlling the loop?

props.command: If one endpoint absorbs tools, structured outputs, and server tools, where is the real seam — the line past which you stop controlling the loop?

beats.narration: A team ships three separate API wrappers — one for plain responses, one for structured outputs, one for tool calls. They discover later that all three hit the same endpoint with different parameters. The tier difference they were managing wasn't surface-level — it was loop ownership: does the code control the next call, or does the agent?

Every Claude API call goes through POST /v1/messages. The model ID, the messages array, the system prompt, the max_tokens cap — these are the four required shapes. Tool definitions and response_format are parameter flags on the same request. There is no separate structured-output API. There is no separate tool-calling API. One surface, one message shape, progressive feature unlock via parameters.

manim.description: Single POST /v1/messages box. Parameters branch off: model, messages[], system, tools[], response_format. Branches appear on cue (karaoke). Terracotta marks the one surface.

beats.narration: Three supporting endpoints orbit Messages. Files: upload binary data too large for inline — PDFs, images, reference docs — and get back a file_id you embed in messages. Batches: submit arrays of requests processed asynchronously at lower cost, a 50% discount at scale. Streaming: server-sent events for incremental token delivery. These aren't alternatives to Messages — they extend how Messages receives or delivers data.

artifactLines: Files API — upload large docs; get file_id; embed in messages[]
Batches API — async arrays of requests; 50% cost discount at scale
Streaming — server-sent events; incremental token delivery
None of these replace Messages — they extend how it receives/delivers

beats.narration: The workflow tier: you own the loop

card.copy: The workflow tier: you own the loop

beats.narration: The workflow tier is when your code decides what happens next. Tool-use: the model says 'call search()'; your code executes it and feeds the result back. Structured outputs: the model returns JSON your code parses. In both cases, your code is driving — it decides whether to keep looping, what the next message is, when to stop. The model is a very capable function call inside your while loop.

beats.narration: The agent seam: the four-question test

card.copy: The agent seam: the four-question test

beats.narration: The seam between workflow and agent: four questions. Does your code decide what the next tool call is, or does the model? Does your code interpret the output, or does the model? Does your code hold the conversation state, or does the model? Is the next action determined before or after the model response? Workflow tier: your code drives all four. Agent tier: the model drives all four. A hybrid means you're managing the boundary manually.

manim.description: Four questions as a checklist. WORKFLOW column: your code checks all four. AGENT column: model checks all four. Questions appear on cue. Terracotta highlights the shift at the seam.

beats.narration: Crossing the wall to Managed Agents

card.copy: Crossing the wall to Managed Agents

beats.narration: Managed Agents is a different surface — not a parameter flag on Messages. When you graduate a task: the infrastructure handles conversation state, parallel tool execution, and resource limits. You define the starting instruction and the tools; the orchestration layer handles the loop. The crossing point is when you stop wanting to own the loop and start wanting the infrastructure to manage it on your behalf.

artifactLines: NOT a Messages parameter — a separate surface
You supply: starting instruction + tool definitions
Infrastructure handles: state, parallel execution, resource limits
Crossing point: when you stop wanting to own the loop
Graduate when: cost-of-error test fails for manual orchestration
props.sparkLine: Graduate when the loop is no longer yours to manage.

beats.narration: A support tool starts as one classify call — Messages, plain response. Adds tool use to look up an order — still Messages, your code drives the loop. Moves overnight triage to the Batches endpoint — async, same Messages shape. Fails a cost-of-error test for an end-to-end sandbox refund — graduate to Managed Agents. Four stages, one endpoint, one wall.

manim.description: Linear progression: CLASSIFY → TOOL-USE → BATCH → AGENT. Each step appears on cue. Terracotta marks the wall between BATCH and AGENT. Labels: 'your code drives' on left, 'infrastructure drives' on right of the wall.

Files / Batches / Streaming: orbit layers, not alternatives
Workflow tier: your code drives the loop
Agent seam: four questions — who decides next action?
Managed Agents: infrastructure drives; you supply instruction + tools
Locate your task on the ladder before choosing the tier
